question: The perimeter of a rhombus is 100 cm. If one of the diagonals measures 14 cm, then the area of the rhombus is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Side (s) = Perimeter ÷ 4 = 100 ÷ 4 = 25 cm.

One half-diagonal (d₁/2) = 14 ÷ 2 = 7 cm.

The other half-diagonal (d₂/2) = √(25² − 7²) = √(625 − 49) = 24 cm.

Area of Rhombus = 2 × (d₁/2) × (d₂/2) = 2 × 7 × 24 = 336 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 336 cm².**
